newsitem.title: USA: Florida citrus prepares for near-freezing temps.
newsitem.headline: Florida citrus prepares for near-freezing temps.

text.p: Florida citrus growers planned to spray trees with a light coating of water to insulate them against chilly weekend temperatures expected to hover near freezing, Florida Citrus Mutual said.
"The temperatures forecast for this weekend don't pose a real problem for our industry," said Bobby McKown, executive vice president of the grower cooperative.
"Our grower members are certainly on alert and will be spraying the trees to raise the temperature so any frost won't settle on the leaves."
Early Friday, temperatures in central Florida's orange-growing fields dropped to as low as 35 degrees Fahrenheit.
National Weather Service forecasts call for weekend lows to dip to "near-freezing" early Sunday morning, McKown said.
Most of the citrus fruit has already been harvested in the state's northern tier of fields, he said.
